To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the amplification stimulator HSAG-1 has multiple positive and negative elements and that the intact configuration of the positive elements in HSAG-1 was required for optimal amplification stimulation.

the HSAG-1 element contains both positive- and negative-regulatory elements that influence its activity in gene amplification, and that HSAG-1 activity is due to its unique configuration and not to the presence of a single positive element.

HSAG-1 contains multiple positive- and multiple negative-acting elements, the combination of which is necessary to achieve the maximal activity, and that HSAG- 1-like sequences are not uncommon in the mammalian cell genome.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the isolation and characterization of a mammalian sequence, HSAG-1 (for HSAG for human sequence activating gene), that stimulates the amplification of a linked marker gene in CHO and other cell lines.
the identification of the sequence elements that affect the frequency of amplification and the mechanisms by which these elements function.
the identification of elements that can stimulate gene amplification and the elucidation of their mechanism of action.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSAG-1 contains multiple positive and negative-acting sequences that interact in a complex manner to produce a stimulatory effect on gene amplification.
the HSAG-1 sequence contains a number of elements, both positive and negative, that are necessary for the activity.
the HSAG-1 element contains multiple positive- and at least one negative-acting elements that influence amplification activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HSAG-1 contains a complex array of positive- and negative-regulating sequences that are required for the optimal amplification stimulatory response.
the amplification stimulator HSAG-1 has a modular structure with a minimum of two positive-acting regions that can be separated by at least 1.2 kb.

the activity of HSAG- 1 was not due to a single sequence element but to the presence of several sequence and structural elements, the precise combination of which was required for maximum amplification activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there may be multiple elements that can stimulate gene amplification.
HSAG-1 and HSAG-2, the most active elements we have tested, are not likely to contain the minimal sequence requirements for gene amplification.
there is a lot of variability in the sequences and structures that can stimulate gene amplification.
